subject: OmniHealth AZ1 egress starvation — urgent escalation and cross-region plan
messages:
From: Jenna Clarke <jenna@omnihealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@omnihealth.com
Date: 2027-03-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: OmniHealth — AZ1 egress starvation causing timeouts

Markus / Redwood team,

We just started seeing a sharp increase in 5xxs and client timeouts across our production traffic hitting AZ1 (us-east-az1). Error rate jumped from ~0.8% to ~12% within the last 8 minutes; median latency has doubled and p95 is spiking above 2.4s. This is impacting our checkout flows — we have multiple merchants reporting failed transactions.

What we see on our side: short bursts of 502/504, long tails on token issuance calls, and repeated retry traffic causing queue pileups. Our SLOs are in jeopardy and CS is fielding escalations. Can you confirm whether this is an infra-side egress networking issue, KV cache saturation, or something else? We need an immediate mitigation (cross-region steering or capacity augmentation) and a timeline.

Attaching a short sample of request traces and a few error responses. Please treat as P0 and advise next steps ASAP.

— Jenna Clarke
Head of Site Reliability, OmniHealth
jenna@omnihealth.com
+1 415-555-0132

Attachments: p0-debug-log-0319.txt (tail), az1-metrics-snapshot-0814.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Clarke <jenna@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-19T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: OmniHealth — AZ1 egress starvation causing timeouts

Jenna — thank you for the heads up and sorry for the customer impact. We are treating this as P0.

Immediate steps we are taking (timeline below):
- Stand up an incident bridge now (link: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/abc123).
- Ops team will run an AZ1 health check and surface any egress/network anomalies.
- If we confirm infrastructure congestion or KV cache contention, we will kick a controlled traffic steer to us-west-2 as a short-term fallback while we remediate.

Can you share whether OmniHealth can accept a progressive steering of traffic to us-west-2 for up to 60 minutes if needed? That will prevent checkout failures while we investigate.

ETA: we expect initial findings within 10 minutes and will propose a mitigation action within 15 minutes. Rafael / Kim / Priyom are on it and will post updates to the bridge.

— Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-19T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: URGENT: OmniHealth — AZ1 egress starvation causing timeouts

Update from runtime / infra:
- Observed: node-level egress saturation on several AZ1 hosts; sustained CPU cycles on the KV cache process and growing request queue depth. Token cache hit-rate has declined ~18% over last 6 minutes which aligns with the retry amplification Jenna reported.
- Network fabric: initial fabric telemetry shows elevated egress queuing for the AZ1 egress layer but no immediate packet-loss spike.

Proposed immediate mitigations (recommended):
1) Open a controlled drift: steer 30% of OmniHealth production traffic to us-west-2 within 5 minutes to relieve pressure and validate stability.
2) Reserve additional Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 (hot-standby) to accept traffic, pre-warm KV caches with critical prefixes.
3) Engage the autoscaler to increase AZ1 worker capacity by 15% as a temporary measure while we evaluate root cause.

Risks: progressive steering reduces error surface but may increase cross-region latency for some user segments. Full drain requires Exec sign-off because of cost/SLAs.

I attached the cross-region drain playbook and a snapshot of AZ1 metrics for the last 20 minutes. I will join the bridge to run through the steps.

— Rafael
(Operations Lead)

Attachments: cross-region-drain-playbook.pdf, az1-metrics-snapshot-0814.csv
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-19T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: URGENT: OmniHealth — AZ1 egress starvation causing timeouts

Rishi — quick ask for executive approval:
- We recommend immediate progressive steering (30% -> monitor 10 min -> escalate to 60% or full if needed). This will trigger cross-region billing (approx. 2.5x unit token cost for routed tokens) and may require a short one-time credit conversation with OmniHealth. Rafael will own the ops steps.

Request: please sign off on the cross-region steering and a discretionary one-time 10% credit for the impacted window if OmniHealth's final impact exceeds 30 minutes. We will keep legal and finance in the loop but need a quick thumb on the call to proceed.

Link to HubSpot incident: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-3291 (OmniHealth incident).

— Kim

Date: 2027-03-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Action plan: progressive steer to us-west-2 + exec bridge details

Jenna — quick update and confirmed plan: thank you for the detailed traces. Exec has given provisional approval for a controlled cross-region steer. Here is the play:

T+0 (now): open incident bridge — https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/abc123 (Ops + CS + Omni SREs).
T+5m: steer 30% of production traffic to us-west-2 (pre-warmed nodes). Monitor for 10 minutes for error-rate and p95 latency.
T+15m: if error-rate does not fall below 1.5% and p95 below 1.0s, increase to 60%.
T+30m: if issues persist, move to full redirect and engage long-run remediation plan + post-incident credit discussion.

We have reserved hot-standby capacity in us-west-2 and pre-warmed critical KV prefixes for OmniHealth. Rafael is executing the first step now.

One-time customer impact credit: we have provisional approval to offer a discretionary credit (up to 10% of March usage) if the outage window exceeds 30 minutes; finance/legal will finalize wording after the bridge.

I will post playbook attachments and a short summary to HubSpot after the bridge. Apologies again — we will treat this as top priority until fully resolved.

— Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
markus@redwood.ai
